counterexample.interpretation: Even commuting positive Hessians and orthogonal anchor gradients do not imply order invariance. A then B worsens objective A relative to the anchor, while the fixed anchored delta sum improves both toy objectives.
counterexample.orthogonal_under: Euclidean, H_A, H_B and H_A+H_B metrics at the anchor.

original_derivation.fixed_delta_addition: theta0+alpha*delta_A+beta*delta_B is permutation invariant in exact arithmetic when both deltas are fixed at the same anchor. This identity makes no performance guarantee and is separate from finite-precision accumulation.
original_derivation.order_convention: AB means A first, then B: T_B^beta(T_A^alpha(theta)).
proof_steps: Subtract the two exact Euler compositions; the two anchor-gradient terms cancel.
Expand g_A(theta-beta*g_B) and g_B(theta-alpha*g_A) with the integral Hessian remainder.
A Lipschitz Hessian bounds each gradient remainder by rho*norm(update)^2/2; multiply by the outer step size and use the triangle inequality.
original_derivation.quadratic_exactness: For quadratic losses rho_A=rho_B=0; the displayed difference is exact at every theta.
original_derivation.quadratic_global_commutation_conditions: For nonzero alpha*beta, equality for every theta requires H_B*H_A=H_A*H_B and H_B*a=H_A*b.
original_derivation.remainder_assumptions: H_A,H_B are Lipschitz with constants rho_A,rho_B along their respective straight update segments; alpha,beta are nonnegative.

primary_paper_context.relevance: Defines fixed task vectors by subtracting shared pretrained weights from fine-tuned weights; addition of fixed vectors is the composition considered here.

scope_limits: Toy quadratic objectives only; no neural model/data/quality measurements.
